newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Podravka plans to reduce borrowing costs.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Podravka plans to reduce borrowing costs.

text.p: Croatia's loss-making food concern Podravka d.d. said on Thursday it planned to swap some 350 million kuna in short-term loans to Croatian banks for more favourable liabilities so as to reduce borrowing costs.
"Restructuring of liabilities is part of our programme of restructuring for a profitable growth," finance director Franjo Juric told Reuters by telephone.
The aim is to improve term-structure and bring the average interest rate down to between eight and 10 percent from over 30 percent, Juric said.
Roughly one third of Podravka's old loans have already been replaced, partly by four-year bonds and partly by medium-term credits from foreign banks and Zagrebacka Banka, he said.
"New loans are for about five years at 10 percent on average," Juric said.
The interest Podravka is paying for the remaining loans fell to around 20 percent as a result of this summer's decline in interbank rates.
Even so, Juric said such a cost was way too high for Podravka's business and the company aimed to replace these loans by cheaper foreign or domestic borrowing which is still being negotiating.
It hoped to finalise the exchange by the end of this year. The majority owner, the Croatian government, was expected to guaratee some of the new liabilities, he said.
Podravka, based in Koprivnica in rural northern Croatia, is one of the country's main exporters.
Despite sales of 2.25 billion kuna in 1995, it posted a consolidated loss of 135 million because of unprofitable production in some outlets and high financing costs.

But thanks to rumours about a deal with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and an eventual foreign flotation, Podravka's shares have risen steadily over the past three months, closing Wednesday at 285 kuna on Zagreb's bourse.
